create_document.description: Add a new document to an index. Provide a Document ID to control the id (the action fails if that id already exists; use Update document to change an existing one), or leave it blank to let Elasticsearch generate one.
create_document.display_str_template: Create a document in the index '{0}'.
create_document.name: create_document

parameters.description: Name of the index to add the document to (for example 'products'). Elasticsearch creates the index automatically if it does not exist yet.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: The document to store, as field/value pairs (for example, name: 'Wireless Headphones', price: 79.99).
parameters.name: document

parameters.description: Optional unique id for the new document. When blank, Elasticsearch generates one and returns it.
parameters.name: document_id

index.description: Index the document was written to

delete_document.description: Delete a document from an index by its Document ID.
delete_document.name: delete_document

parameters.description: The index the document lives in.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: The document's unique id within the index.
parameters.name: document_id

index.description: Index the document was deleted from

get_document.description: Retrieve a single document from an index by its Document ID.
get_document.name: get_document

parameters.description: The index the document lives in.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: The document's unique id within the index.
parameters.name: document_id

search_documents.description: Find documents in an index by words they contain, by the value of one field, or both, such as every order whose status is pending. Leave both empty to list the index's documents. Returns up to 100, sorted by a field you choose or by how well they match.
search_documents.name: search_documents

parameters.description: The index the document lives in.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: Words to look for anywhere in the documents, such as wireless headphones. Every word must appear. Leave it empty to match on a field alone, or to list documents.
parameters.name: search_text

parameters.description: Only documents whose value in this field matches Value, such as status. Use dots for a field inside another, such as customer.email.
parameters.name: field

parameters.description: The value Field must have, such as pending. Needed when Field is filled in.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: A field to put the documents in order by, such as created_at or price. Leave it empty to put the best matches first.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Which end of Sort by comes first.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: The most documents to return, from 1 to 100.
parameters.name: limit

documents.description: The documents found, each with its index, document_id, score (how well it matched) and document (its stored fields)

index.description: The index the document is in

score.description: How well it matched; empty when sorted by a field

total.description: How many documents match in all, which can be more than were returned

update_document.description: Update a document by its Document ID. The fields you provide are merged into the stored document, leaving its other fields unchanged.
update_document.name: update_document

parameters.description: Name of the index the document lives in (for example 'products'). With 'Create if missing' on, a new index is created automatically if it does not exist yet.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: The document's unique id within the index.
parameters.name: document_id

parameters.description: The fields to add or change, as field/value pairs (for example, price: 69.99). Fields you omit are left as they are.
parameters.name: document

parameters.description: When on, a document that does not exist yet is created from these fields instead of failing.
parameters.name: upsert

result.description: Elasticsearch write result, e.g. 'updated' or 'noop' when the fields already matched

description: Create, read, update, search and delete documents in your Elasticsearch indices, and start a workflow when a document is added.

elasticsearch_new_document_trigger.description: Runs when a document is added to an Elasticsearch index, found by checking for documents past the highest value seen so far of a field every new document gets, such as created_at. Documents without that field are never seen, and documents already in the index don't trigger it.

output.document_id: The new document's id, for Get, Update or Delete document.
output.field: The order field the trigger watches.
output.index: The index it was added to.

parameters.description: The index to watch, such as orders.
parameters.name: index

parameters.description: A field every new document gets, whose value grows with each one, such as a created_at time or an increasing number. It must be a date, number or keyword field; for text, use its .keyword version, such as order_number.keyword.
parameters.name: field
